50-028.r: Agriculture in India → a means of livelihood: employs most of the workforce but adds only a small share of GDP.

50-029.r: Pulses in India → about 90% of area rainfed (only 12.7% irrigated then; 16.1% in 2011-12); pulse share of area did not double.

50-030.r: Largest chemical fertilizer users (2013-14): Uttar Pradesh 3842.04, Andhra Pradesh 3119.43 thousand tonnes. In 2024-25: Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh.

50-031.r: Highest nitrogen among green manures → Cow pea (Lobia) 0.49%; Sunhemp 0.43%, Dhaincha 0.42%, Guar 0.34%.

50-032.r: Green manure crop for newly improved arid land → Lobia (cow pea).

50-033.r: Balanced fertilizers → raise production, improve fertilizer-use efficiency and grain quality, maintain soil productivity → all of these.

50-034.r: High agricultural productivity in South India → coastal Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh (also Surat in Gujarat, Satara and Kolhapur in Maharashtra).

50-035.r: Richest in replenishable groundwater (2011) → Uttar Pradesh 72.84 billion cubic m/year; MP 35.90, AP 27.80, West Bengal 25.89.

50-036.r: Pioneer state in introducing contract farming in India → Punjab.

50-037.r: Green agriculture → integrated pest management, integrated nutrient supply, integrated natural resource (water) management, suitable crop varieties.

50-038.r: Globalization (1991) impact on Indian agriculture: emphasis on cash crops, growing income inequality, subsidy cuts; climate change is NOT such an impact.

50-039.r: Seed Village Concept → train farmers in quality seed production so quality seeds reach others on time at affordable cost.

50-040.r: Agmark → quality certification mark under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937; in use since 1938.

50-041.r: Landholdings (Agriculture Census 2015-16): marginal less than 1 ha; small 1-2; semi-medium 2-4; medium 4-10; large more than 10 ha.

50-042.r: Conservation Agriculture → minimum tillage, crop residue cover on soil, crop rotation/sequencing (answer 2, 4, 5); not avoiding plantation crops.

50-043.r: Paths to higher farm productivity: efficient irrigation, quality seeds, pesticides, fertilizers → all work, so answer (e) 'more than one'.

50-044.r: Agriculture Census 2015-16: small + marginal farmers 86.2% of farmers but 47.3% of land; Maharashtra third by farmer numbers; Rajasthan first by farm area.

51-001.r: Green Revolution (New Agricultural Strategy) → began 1966-67; first stage covered Haryana, Punjab and western Uttar Pradesh.
51-001.c: The book prints (b) Seventies, but its own date 1966-67 falls in the Sixties (the 7th decade of the 20th century), so (c) Sixties fits better.

51-002.r: 'Evergreen Revolution' → term of M.S. Swaminathan (Father of India's Green Revolution): raising productivity in perpetuity without ecological harm.

51-003.r: Norman Ernest Borlaug, Father of the Green Revolution (world) → USA (born 1914, Cresco, Iowa); developed semi-dwarf wheat in Mexico.
51-003.t: Don't confuse: Borlaug worked in Mexico but was from the USA.

51-005.r: Dr. M.S. Swaminathan → 'Father of India's Green Revolution' (high-yielding wheat varieties).

51-006.r: Green Revolution → High Yielding Variety programme (HYV seeds, more fertilizer, farm equipment); began in India 1966-67 with Rockefeller Foundation help.
hi: High yielding variety (उच्च उपज वाली किस्म)

51-008.r: Green Revolution → mainly wheat production (output rose 2.5 times); began 1966-67; credit: Norman Borlaug and M.S. Swaminathan.

51-009.r: Highest beneficiary of Green Revolution in production and productivity → Wheat, then rice.

51-011.r: Maximum progress after Independence → Wheat production (driven by the Green Revolution, 1966-67).

51-012.r: Main crop of Green Revolution → Mexican wheat (from Borlaug's International Maize and Wheat centre); 1960s: HYV seeds, fertilizers, irrigation.

51-013.r: Green Revolution → wheat yield touched record 2000 kg/ha (three times earlier); yield in 2024-25: 3595 kg/ha.

51-014.r: Second Green Revolution aims: extend seed-water-fertilizer technology to left-out areas; integrate cropping with animal husbandry, social forestry, fishing (answer 2 and 4).

51-015.r: Green Revolution components (after 1965): HYV seeds, irrigation, rural electrification, rural roads and marketing → all four.

51-016.r: Green Revolution → raised food grain output (A true) and worsened regional disparities (R true); R does not explain A.

51-017.r: Rainbow Revolution (National Agricultural Policy, 28 July 2000) → covers Green, White, Yellow, Blue and other revolutions → all the above.

51-018.r: Food production → Green; Milk → White; Fisheries → Blue; Fertilizers → Grey Revolution.

51-019.r: Pink Revolution → Onion; Black → Petroleum (crude oil); Red → Tomato and Meat; Blue → Fisheries; Yellow → Oilseed.

51-021.r: Golden Revolution → Horticulture and Honey; Grey → Fertilizers; Yellow → Oilseeds; Black → Petroleum.
51-021.h: Grey = grey fertilizer sacks; Black = black oil; Yellow = yellow mustard flowers.

51-022.r: Wrong pair: Blue — Poultry; Blue Revolution is fisheries/aquaculture. Golden → Horticulture; White → Milk; Green → Agriculture.

51-025.r: Blue Revolution in India → Pisciculture (commercial fish rearing in tanks/enclosures).

51-026.r: Blue Revolution in India → Pisciculture (fish production).
51-026.t: Don't confuse Pisciculture (fish) with Sericulture, Floriculture or Horticulture.

51-028.r: Zero Till Seed-cum-Fertilizer Drill → developed at G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar; sows directly after paddy harvest.

51-029.r: Wrong pair: Blue — Poultry; Blue Revolution is fisheries. White → Milk; Green → Food grains; Golden → Horticulture.

51-030.r: Not a commercial crop → Bajra (millet); sugarcane, cotton and banana are commercial (cash) crops.

52-001.r: Rabi crops → sown October-November (e.g. mustard, masoor); Kharif crops → sown June-July with first rains, harvested October-November.

52-007.r: Odd one out → Wheat (Rabi); Paddy, Jowar, Maize are Kharif crops.

52-008.r: Wheat needs moderate temperature (10-25°C) and moderate rain (50-75 cm, evenly spread); grown on 32.80 million ha (2024-25).

52-009.r: Cash crops: sugarcane, cotton, jute, tobacco, oilseeds, bananas; wheat and rice are food crops.

52-011.r: 1998 → India signed an agreement with Australia to import 15 lakh tonnes of wheat.

52-012.r: Wheat output 2020-21 (4th advance estimates) → 109.5 million tonnes; 2024-25 → 117.94 million tonnes.

52-013.r: Top three wheat states when asked: Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana. In 2024-25: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab.
52-013.t: Recent data puts Madhya Pradesh second; Uttar Pradesh stays first.

52-015.r: Largest wheat producer 2015-16 → Uttar Pradesh 25.43 Mt (MP 17.69, Punjab 16.08); in 2024-25 UP 35.65 Mt.

52-016.r: Maximum wheat production → Uttar Pradesh (2024-25: 35.65 Mt), then Madhya Pradesh 24.51, Punjab 17.99.

52-017.r: Mahi Sugandha → a Basmati rice variety (long, non-sticky grains after cooking).
